The Data Recipient agrees to process the Data only for the following purposes agreed with the HSCIC: 
To derive performance and quality indicators for Learning Disability services, in order to drive improvements in the services and to identify where good/poor practice is taking place. Analysis will be carried out by NHS England analysts. Identifiable data will only be accessed and analysed by the named analysts covered by the Section 251 agreement. Any analysis carried out will not include identifiable data, and small numbers will be suppressed.
Section 251 approvals CAG 8-02 (a)/2011, CAG 8-02 (b)/2011, CAG 8-02 (c)/2011 state that approval is given subject to data collected before 10/12/2014 is excluded from s251 legal basis cover. The approval also states that data relating to a third party in any way is also excluded from s251 cover.
As a result of these s251 caveats, this will be covered under section 254 of the Health and Social Care Act 2012 therefore s251 becomes a secondary legal basis.
Objective for processing: 
Data will not be stored, processed or in any other way accessible by a third party. Data will be stored in the secure storage that was set up when NHS England managed this data collection themselves.
Data will be analysed to produce aggregate level reports, to allow operational managers to work with challenged organisations to improve delivery and performance against key national indicators. Patient level data will be accessible only to those named individuals that have been given access to the secure data storage, and will only be accessed in the safe haven environment set up for this purpose.
Processing activities: 
Outputs will be commissioner-level analysis, used for internal management purposes. There are six key performance indicators (patient stock, admissions, discharges, patients without a care coordinator, patients not on a CCG register and patients without a CPA review in the last 26 weeks) to which NHS England will hold commissioners to account – this management information will allow local operational managers to ensure commissioners are delivering these indicators, and to intervene when they are not. In addition further performance/quality indicators based on this data set are in development, such as indicators on length of stay and readmission rates. 
Analysis will not be published in journals or be used in relation to clinical trials, nor used for direct marketing. Small numbers will be suppressed. Performance dashboards and other analysis will be used internally and with commissioners once the Information has been published by HSCIC. These will be in aggregated form only. Quarterly data sets will be used for any external reporting of the national indicators. The HSCIC’s guidance on suppression of small numbers will be followed.
Specific outputs expected, including target date(s): 
The data will give insight at organisation (provider/commissioner) level, the benefits will be that operational managers will have an evidence base through which to drive improvements in services and patient experience. As soon as this evidence base is available (within weeks of receiving the data) actions can be taken to begin these improvements. Without this evidence base targeted work to improve services and patient experience cannot take place.
